newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-MIM says native title claim lodged.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-MIM says native title claim lodged.

text.p: MIM Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday a native title claim had been formally lodged over an area in Queensland that includes its Ernest Henry copper-gold project but the company said it would not affect the right to mine.
"The native title claim will not affect the right of Ernest Henry Mining Pty Ltd (EHM) to mine the deposit," MIM said.
"Construction is well advanced and production is due to commence in the second half of next year," the company said.

The claim had been lodged by Mitakoodi Juhnjlar Aboriginal Corporation, MIM said. EHM will continue to work with Aboriginal groups to maximise benefits for local people from the region's economic developments, the MIM statement said.

The A$350 million Ernest Henry project, owned 51 percent by MIM and 49 percent by Savage Resources Ltd, is expected to be producing at an annual rate of 95,000 tonnes of copper and 120,000 ounces of gold.
MIM said last week that Suncave Pty Ltd, a firm associated with Aboriginal interests, was seeking A$120 million to ensure no native title claim was made on the mine or water supply.
However, MIM said on Wednesday it would not negotitate on this basis. "We're playing a very straight bat," Collin Myers, MIM's general manager corporate affairs, told Reuters.
"We told Suncave that we thought this was an inappropriate basis to seek benefits for the Aboriginal people of the region," Myers said.
More appropriate initiatives were in commercial involvement, contracts, employment, educational training and supporting the Aboriginal Corporation, he said.
